list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.6_DE 1.54.26
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.6_DE 1.54.26
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **A track queued twice no longer takes the app down.** The crash dump (`~/.vivimusic/crash.log`, 10 Oct 20:46) is one line long and names it: `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Key "pSVbF6DGH9U" was already used`, thrown from a `LazyColumn`'s own measure pass. Both queue lists (the player's queue panel and the full queue screen) were keyed by `item.videoId` alone and gave the reorder base the same key, so the same track in the queue twice - one "Play next" on a track already queued is enough - asked Compose for two rows with one key and closed the window. The key is the track plus how many times it has already appeared (`List<String>.withOccurrences`, `Components.kt`), which is unique and still follows a row while the queue is dragged into a new order; a local playlist's own song list, the other list that can hold a track twice, got the same treatment. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin`, `:desktop:compileTestKotlin` and `:desktop:ltRoomRenderCheck` (`room (host) ink=342428`, `room (guest) ink=293228`, `OK`) all pass with the new keys. **Watch:** queue the same song twice and open the queue: two rows, no crash, and a drag must still carry the row it picked up.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **Listen Together: the relay moved to the top of the screen, and the connection buttons that duplicated it are gone.** The relay address was the first row of the settings section at the bottom, at the far end of the screen from the connection it describes, and the room also carried **Disconnect** and **Reconnect** in its own action row on top of the same pair in the status card. The relay is now the connection card's own row, above everything else: the server's **name** on its own line, its address underneath, and the phone's picker behind **Choose server** (the two public relays with their location and operator, plus the custom address field). The settings section keeps the account, the three switches, the blocked list and the log viewer, and no longer shows an address at all. **Disconnect** and **Reconnect** are gone from both places - the client reconnects on its own when the socket drops, so the pair only invited a press the status line was already reporting - and the room's own row is down to **Request sync** and **Leave room**. **Connect** stays, because in the disconnected state there is nothing to drop. **Watch:** the top card must name the server in use and offer the picker, the settings must not repeat the address, and the room row must be two buttons.
- [DE] **Listen Together: the room code card wears the Copy code button's own shape.** The hero card was one solid accent block (`primaryContainer`) holding the code and the two copy buttons, so the container and the buttons were the same colour and neither the code nor the labels stood out. It is a surface with a one-pixel accent border now, the code in the accent colour and every label on the surface, and the two buttons are the only filled shapes in it.
- [DE] **Listen Together: the Suggestions section says how a suggestion is made.** A small line under the title, `⋮ Suggest · Paste a YouTube link or video ID`, built from the two strings the song menu and the field already use (`lt_suggest`, `lt_suggest_placeholder`), so it costs no new translation and both roles see it: the host reads where suggestions come from, the guest reads what the field takes.
- [DE] **Listen Together: the avatars are drawn with the high-quality filter.** The bundled pictures are 512x512 and are drawn at 36 to 46 dp; the default filter samples them without mipmaps, which is what made a reduced face look pixelated (reported as pixelated on the desktop only - the phone draws its own copies from the same files). `LtAvatar` asks for `FilterQuality.High` now, so the small circle is a smooth reduction of the big file. **Measured:** `:desktop:ltRoomRenderCheck` renders all three avatar kinds (initial, picture, and the last picture) and still reports them drawing at 5115 px of ink each.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.6_DE-1.54.26: a track queued twice no longer crashes the app, and Listen Together keeps one server row and two room buttons

---
This release was built automatically from commit `0ff85277e06eacb83dbd2a7ebb28fcb680572712`.

list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.6_DE 1.54.25
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The custom colour is one round wheel, on the right of the section.** The picker was three horizontal HSV bars (hue, saturation, brightness) stacked under the palette; it is one round wheel now, placed to the right of the hex field and the **Add to palette** button. Hue runs around the rim, saturation comes out of the white centre, and the marker sits exactly on the picked colour - its angle is the hue, its distance the saturation - so one drag picks both. The disc is drawn from two gradients on a `Canvas`, a sweep for the hue and a radial white-to-transparent for the saturation, and darkened to the current brightness, so it always shows the colour being selected; one gesture loop tracks the press and every movement, the shape the bars used after issue #61 (`detectTapGestures` never returns, so the call after it was dead code and the surface only reacted on the release), which keeps the marker under the pointer. Brightness stays adjustable as a slim vertical strip beside the wheel (full colour at the top, black at the bottom) whose tooltip is the translated `brightness`; the three bars and the `GradientBar` composable they were drawn with are gone. **Measured:** the new `./gradlew :desktop:colorWheelRenderCheck` renders the real `ThemeSection` into an off-screen `ImageComposeScene` with the picker open and reads the pixels back: the wheel is a round 220x220 disc of 37155 px of ink (`wheel blob: 220x220px, 37155px of ink, at 746,928`), its rim reads red `(255,52,53)` at 3 o'clock, yellow-green `(152,255,52)` at the bottom, cyan `(50,254,255)` at the left and blue `(151,50,255)` at the top, its centre reads white `(253,254,255)`, the marker follows the accent the screen opens on (right `(962,1037)` for a red accent, lower-left `(801,1130)` for a green one), the strip runs from `(0,236,0)` at the top to `(0,128,0)` half way down, and no wide gradient band is left on the screen. **Open sub-item:** the wheel sits inside the picker section rather than beside the palette, and how the screen reads on a real window is unverified here: the check proves what is drawn, not how it looks.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.6_DE-1.54.25: the custom colour is one round wheel, and the APK version moves to 6.0.8.6

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.24
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.24
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **A guest's transport is drawn disabled instead of only explained, and the whole app agrees on it.** 1.54.23 made the lock *answer* (the press showed the room's own sentence) and deliberately left every control enabled, on the reasoning that "a disabled control explains nothing". The owner asked for the opposite, so the controls are now drawn disabled as well — and both halves are kept: `transportLocked()` sets `enabled = false` and `dimmedWhenLocked()` (0.38 alpha) makes it read as unavailable, while the sentence the lock already produced stays as the control's tooltip, so a press that a keyboard shortcut or a media key still routes through `PlayerController` continues to be answered. It is one state read in every player surface rather than the two places that had it: the full player (seek bar, previous / play / next), the docked bottom bar, the mini player, the floating Now Playing widget, a song's `⋮` menu (`Play next` and `Add to queue`), an album's / artist's / playlist's context menu (`Play all`, `Shuffle all`, `Play next`, `Add to queue` — `DetailMenuEntry` grew the `enabled` flag), the queue's **Clear queue**, and now the **tray icon's right-click menu**, whose three transport rows are drawn greyed by the same flag (`TrayActions.transportEnabled`) and rebuilt the moment the role changes. Shuffle and repeat stay live on purpose: the lock never covered them (`PlayerController` does not refuse them), so greying them would be a lie in the other direction. The one place a control cannot be greyed is the operating system's own — the Windows media-key hook and the macOS "Now Playing" tile and media keys — and there the lock's own sentence is the answer, which is what those paths already get. **Watch:** as a guest, every one of those controls must be grey and inert while the track keeps playing, the tooltip must read the room's sentence, and Space / the media keys must still answer with it instead of doing nothing. **Open sub-item:** no guest room can be opened here (the relay needs two accounts), so this is compile-verified plus the render check below; the surfaces are all fed by the one `ListenTogetherGate.locked` the manager already kept in step.
- [DE] **The Google sign-in window opens as many times as it is pressed, in one session.** 1.54.23 closed two of the three doors — the permanent `unavailable` flag and the window a timeout left open — and the owner came back with the same sentence, *"io la DEVO potere aprire quante volte voglio a sessione"*, because the third one was still there: the window held **one** callback, the one of the request that opened it, and a second request arriving while it was up was answered with `return true` and no callback at all. The sign-in screen sets "waiting for the window" before it calls in and clears it only from the callback, so that press left its button disabled for the rest of the session — the window could be opened once, and every later press fell through to the manual paste. Requests are now a list: one that arrives while a window is up **joins** it and is answered with the same capture (`delivering to N waiting request(s)` in `login-debug.log`), `deliver` answers every waiter and clears the flag so the next press opens a new window, and a window that has been silent for 150 s is treated as stuck and replaced by a fresh one instead of blocking the session. The log names every attempt (`window request #3: opening` / `joining the window opened 12s ago` / `the window from 155s ago never answered`). **Watch:** press the button twice in a row in one session and both presses must open a window (the log must show `#1 opening`, then `#2 opening` or `#2 joining`); after a timeout the next press must open a fresh window. **Open sub-item:** needs a display and a real account — this is reasoned from the code and the log lines, not from a completed sign-in.
- [DE] **The localization generator can no longer delete the keys it does not know.** `debug_developer_options`, `disable_developer_options*`, `spotify_open_browser`, `detailed_startup_logs*`, `performance_options*`, `advanced`, `developer_options_unlocked`, `jvm_memory*`, `detailed_playback_logging*`, `hide_custom_apk_download_button*`, `ai_custom_model` and `ai_training_note` — the desktop's own screens, none of which the phone has — were written straight into the generated `Localization_*.kt` files, so **one** `python scripts/generate_desktop_localization.py` deleted all 21 from all 53 tables (measured 10 Oct: `English keys 837 → 815`, the audit's `Missing / leaking 0 → 6514`). They are authored in the generator's `ENGLISH` table and translated in `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_98.py` now, so the generator is the single source again, and it refuses to write a table that would lose an English key it had before. **Measured:** after a full regeneration, `English keys 871`, the audit reports `52 languages, 0 missing or leaking`, and a key-by-key comparison of the tables against the files the generator writes finds **0 keys in the files that the tables do not define** — the check that used to be 21. **Watch:** rerun the generator and then the audit: it must stay at 0.
- [DE] **Two more keys the generator would not have known about, and the sentence a restore failure needs.** `lt_copy_logs` / `lt_clear_logs` (the log viewer's two buttons, mapped onto the phone's own translated `copy` / `clear` resources, plus `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_101.py` for the 33 languages whose resources lack them) and `restore_failed_corrupt`, which the phone defines in its default resources only, so it is authored in all 52 languages in `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_102.py`.
- [DE] **A backup that would not restore now restores, and one that cannot be read says which kind of unreadable it is.** The report is one sentence — *"I tried 3 times to restore it from my backup file but DE is not accepting it and saying failed to restore"* — against a bare `false` that could equally have meant "no file was chosen". Three real refusals were found by driving the actual `BackupManager.import` over the shapes a user's file can have (new `./gradlew :desktop:backupRestoreCheck`): a file with a **byte-order mark** (any editor, or a re-encoding tool: the decoder refuses the whole document, so a perfect JSON failed), an archive whose entries sit **under a folder** (`vivimusic/settings.json`, which is what a re-zipped or tool-made archive looks like — the old code compared the entry name exactly and found nothing), and a **newer-version backup**: a value this build does not know (an enum entry added by a later release, exactly what a downgraded install restores) now falls back to its default instead of failing the file, because the restore reads through its own `Json` with `coerceInputValues`. A settings entry that is present but unreadable is a **failure with a reason** rather than the silent playlists-only restore it used to be called a success, the phone's own archive is refused **by name** (`this is the Android app's backup (settings.preferences_pb), which this edition cannot read` — the most likely file a user hands this screen), and both the row's own Restore and the file-picker Restore now report the outcome instead of opening the "restart to apply" dialog whatever happened. **Measured:** `:desktop:backupRestoreCheck` — a backup this build wrote, the legacy single-JSON file, the same file with a byte-order mark, a folder-prefixed archive and the phone's archive, plus the three real `auto_backup_*.vivide.backup` files on this machine (7 Oct, 6 Oct, 9 Oct), all `import -> true`; a corrupt settings entry answers `false` with `restore_failed_corrupt`. **Watch:** the user's own failing file is not here, so if a restore is still refused, `app.log` now names it (`restore FAILED: <file>: <reason>`). **Open sub-item:** the sign-in-free half of the path (the file picker itself) still needs a display.
- [DE] **The Spotify import's manual-cookie card has one door again.** The screen offered the same decision twice: a `Sign in to Spotify` browser button above the `sp_dc` / `sp_key` paste and the card's own **Log in** under the fields, which is the button the owner asked to keep. The browser button is gone (the card is what the user opens *because* the window did not finish, not another way into it) and the cookie hint below still says where the two values come from. **Watch:** one button on the card, and it must be the one that builds the login from the pasted cookies.

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The Listen Together screen, rebuilt as the phone's screen with the phone's own pictures.** 1.54.23 gave the desktop the *shape* of the phone's options and stood in for its avatars with emoji. Both are gone: the screen is now built from the APK's own Material 3 pieces, and **the avatars are the phone's own image files**, bundled verbatim from the APK (`desktop/src/main/resources/images/avatars/`, `man.png` … `luxury_women.png`) in the phone's exact index order, so `avatar_index` 4 is the same face on both sides instead of "the fourth man" here and a guitar there. The lobby and the room share **one settings section** that is the phone's list: the username and the avatar row (the same fourteen choices, laid out as the phone lays them out), the relay picker with the phone's two public servers named and located (`Hugging Face Sync` · Global · VIVIDH, `ViviMusic Sync Server` · USA · Vividh) plus a custom address, the **blocked users** list with its own Unblock (the list existed to the manager and had no screen), the **log viewer** (copy or clear the client's own log, which the phone has and the desktop kept to itself), and the three switches — auto-approval, volume sync, smart resync — the last two of which the phone greys for a guest, as this does now. The room is one expressive card per idea: the code as a hero card with real Copy code / Copy link buttons and the connected-user count, the users as one grouped card with the host's crown drawn from the room's own `hostId` (never from a per-user flag) and the moderation actions behind a single `⋮` (`Transfer ownership`, `Kick`, `Permanently block` — the phone's long-press dialog as a menu), the join requests with ✓ / ✕, the suggestions (list for the host, the input row for a guest) and the same settings section as the lobby. Every row is still keyed and still deduplicated, because a repeated Compose key is a crash and not a warning. **Measured:** `:desktop:ltRoomRenderCheck` renders the lobby, an avatar of the *initial* kind, one of the *picture* kind, the **last** picture (a missing resource would fall back to the person vector and look plausible) and both room roles off screen: `lobby ink=461257`, the three avatars each 5115 and different from an empty circle, `room (host) ink=405567`, `room (guest) ink=356367`, `OK`. **Watch:** two accounts in one room, one phone and one desktop — the avatars must match, and the host's `⋮` must be able to kick and block. **Open sub-item:** with no display here the look itself is unverified; the render check proves what draws, not how it reads.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **Storage lists the three caches apart, because they are three different costs.** One number covered three things: the audio the extractor cached (`~/.vivimusic/cache`), the lyrics fetched for it (`cache/lyrics`) and the AI's translations of those lyrics (`cache/ai-lyrics`). They have three different lifetimes and three different costs to rebuild — a translation is a paid request, the audio is bandwidth — so each has its own row, its own size and its own **Clear** (`cache_audio`, `cache_lyrics`, `cache_ai_lyrics`, authored in `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_99.py`), and clearing the lyrics or the translations also drops the in-memory copies (`LyricsCache.clearDisk`), which is why the button used to look like it did nothing until a restart. **Watch:** the three sizes must add up to what the disk holds and each Clear must empty only its own directory.
- [DE] **The custom colour is the palette's own last circle, and it follows a preset pick.** The picker was a section of its own further down the screen and its three bars used a plain `remember`, so choosing a colour from the predefined palette left the dial where it had last been dragged. The dial is now drawn as the **last swatch of the palette flow** (right of the predefined colours, wrapping to the next row when the current one is full, with the same selection ring as the others), it opens and closes the bars below it, and the three bars are keyed on the current accent — so picking a preset moves the dial onto it instead of leaving the two disagreeing. **Watch:** pick a preset from the middle of the palette and the dial must move there on its own; open it and the bars must start on the colour in use.

### 🐛 Fixed ([APK])
- [APK] **The phone spends less time drawing lyrics, which is where it was warm for nothing.** The lyrics screen ran two loops that only make sense while the clock is moving, and kept them running while it was not: the metro-lyrics path sat on the **frame clock** (60 recompositions a second, each running `findActiveLineIndices` twice over the whole lyric list), and the second path polled every **8 ms** (125 wake-ups a second). A paused player cannot advance a line, so with the app open on the lyrics screen — which is exactly where a phone is left, screen on, doing nothing — that was CPU and battery spent redrawing a picture that was already correct, and the phone reports it as heat. Both loops now drive the frame clock only while the player is playing **or** a seek is in flight, and idle at a 250 ms tick otherwise (`IDLE_LYRICS_TICK_MS`), re-baselining their clock on resume so a pause never counts as elapsed playback and the position cannot jump. The same treatment went to `LyricsV2`'s frame loop, which is the one the full player uses. **Watch:** with the lyrics open and playback paused, the position and the highlighted line must not move at all, and resuming must not make the karaoke fill jump. **Open sub-item:** a phone is needed to measure temperature; nothing here touches sync — the volume/position polling loops and the relay are untouched, deliberately, because the owner asked for sync to keep its priority.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.24: a guest's controls are greyed, Listen Together wears the phone's own avatars and options, the three caches stand apart, and a backup that can be read restores

---
This release was built automatically from commit `7c2e3fdd60cb23af62f3de07960f5c392aaee566`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.23
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.23
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **Creating a room no longer answers "the room does not exist", and the first room now works.** The report: *"often when I create a room for Listen Together it tells me the room does not exist and I have to create another one."* Nothing was wrong with creating; the socket was talking about a **different** room. The client keeps the last session on disk so a crash mid-room can be resumed, and its `onOpen` sends a `RECONNECT` carrying that session's token. Creating a room while an old session was still stored therefore did two things on the same freshly opened socket: `CREATE_ROOM` (the new room, queued and flushed first) and then, immediately after it, a `RECONNECT` naming the **previous** room. The relay's answer to a room that no longer existed was what the user read — and the second attempt "worked" because the stored token had meanwhile been replaced by the new room's own. `createRoom` and `joinRoom` now drop the stored session first, exactly as the mobile client does (`"clear any existing session to ensure we create a new room instead of reconnecting"`), so the stale `RECONNECT` is never sent. **Watch:** be in a room, close the app, reopen it and create a room: it must open on the first press, with no error line in the room, and the log must not contain a `Reconnecting to room <old code>` between the press and the room appearing.
- [DE] **An approved suggestion lands in the queue, and only once.** The host's approve button dropped the row and sent `APPROVE_SUGGESTION`, then waited for the relay to echo `suggestion_approved` back before inserting anything — an echo the mobile client does not rely on either (it queues the track locally through `LocalSuggestionApproved` → `playNext`). Where the echo does not come back, the approving host saw the suggestion disappear and nothing appear in the queue. The insert now happens in `approveSuggestion`, on the approval itself, and a later echo is dropped through `appliedSuggestions` (keyed by suggestion id) so the same track cannot be queued twice — "play next" is not idempotent. **Watch:** as the host, approve a suggestion from the phone: the track must be the next item in the desktop's queue, exactly once, and approving the same suggestion twice must not queue it twice.
- [DE] **The Google sign-in window can be opened again after a failed attempt.** Two independent reasons a second attempt was impossible. `unavailable` was set by a failure of *one* attempt and never cleared, so a machine where the first attempt failed fell through to the manual paste forever — the report is literally "why can I open the Google login only once". And a capture that reached its 120 s deadline with no session logged `capture timeout` and left the stage open with `windowOpen` still `true`, so the button became inert (it refuses to open a second window) while nothing could ever complete in the one on screen. The flag is retried (a failure sets it, the next press clears it and tries again), and a timeout now closes the window and hands the app a null capture, which is the same path as a user closing it. **Watch:** press *Sign in with Google* after a failed attempt and a window must open again; after a timeout the window must close by itself and the button must be usable.
- [DE] **A guest's play/pause says why it does nothing.** The transport lock was right and silent: `PlayerController` returned from every one of its transport commands while the user was a guest, so the play/pause button was there, looked enabled, and did nothing at all — the report is *"the play/pause button is there but nothing tells me I can't start or stop"*. The lock now answers: the one place every control funnels through (`lockBlocks`) shows the room's own sentence (`lt_guest_note`, "the host controls playback in this room"), which covers the buttons, the keyboard shortcuts, the media keys and the song menus without each of them knowing about the room, and the guest's room screen carries the same sentence at the top, next to the copy buttons, with a lock on it. The mini player draws a lock beside the play button, with the sentence as its tooltip. The controls stay enabled on purpose: a disabled control explains nothing, a press that answers does. **Watch:** as a guest, press play (or Space, or the media key): the track must not move and the message must appear.
- [DE] **The Spotify import's manual-cookie card had two "Show" controls.** The card drew its title row with the Show/Hide label *and* a `TextButton` under it saying the same thing — the two the owner asked about — and the title row's own click was inert while collapsed (it only re-opened an already open card). The header row is now the single toggle. On a machine where the sign-in window cannot be created at all, the card also opens by itself, because there the paste is not the fallback: it is the only way in. **Watch:** one Show/Hide control on the card, it must open and close from a click on its title, and the fields must be there in one click.

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The room screen carries the phone's options, and the avatars travel with them.** The desktop room was thinner than the Android one, so the five things it lacked are here, and the ones that existed were redone in the phone's shape rather than left as they were: **Copiare stanza / link** are real buttons with icons (they were two lines of text that read like labels — the reason the copy button was reported as missing), and the code is copied to the clipboard the moment the room is created, exactly as the phone does; **Espelli e blocca** (the permanent block, which had its state, its API and no button), next to Espelli and Trasferisci host; **Connetti / Disconnetti / Riconnetti**, in the header of the screen, so a half-dead socket is no longer something the app keeps to itself; the **avatar**, picked from the phone's own set and stored as the same `avatar_index`, which now travels in `create_room` / `join_room` / `user_joined` and is drawn for every user in the list (index 0 is the username's initial, 1..13 the emoji stand-ins for the APK's pictures — a desktop user no longer shows up as a bare initial beside phone users who picked one); and a **Settings** section (the relay URL, auto-approve, sync volume, and `smart resync`, which the manager read and no screen showed anywhere) under the phone's own section title. **Measured:** `./gradlew :desktop:ltRoomRenderCheck` renders the lobby, an avatar of each kind and both room roles into an off-screen `ImageComposeScene`; it reports `lobby ink=365544`, the three avatars, `room (host) ink=218632` and `room (guest) ink=222883` and ends with `OK: the lobby, both avatars and both room roles draw, and the two roles differ` — the host and the guest drawing **differently** is what proves the role branches are on screen (the host sees the moderation controls, the guest the lock notice and the suggest box), and the avatars are compared as pictures because a glyph inside the circle replaces circle pixels instead of adding ink. **Watch:** two accounts in one room, one phone and one desktop: the avatars must match on both, and the host's Espelli e blocca must remove the guest from the room.
- [DE] **The login screen says the second attempt is normal, and ERRORS.md says it too.** *"In 90 % of cases the Google login needs two attempts"* — that is what the logs show (`login-debug.log` naming `after www.youtube.com (visit 1/2) … missing=[LOGIN_INFO]` and then a completed session), and it was nowhere the user could see it, so a first attempt that ended in `E1033` read as a broken sign-in. A line above the button now says it (`login_retry_hint`, a desktop-only string authored in `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_97.py` and present in all 52 languages) and the `E1033` row in `ERRORS.md` carries the same instruction: press the button again before falling back to the manual cookie method.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **800x600 keeps the whole interface.** The window used to start giving things away well above that: the density stepped down from 1200 raw dp, the right Now Playing panel was hidden below **1150** and the sidebar collapsed below **980**, so on a 800x600 display both panels were already gone and the interface never appeared in its full shape. The full layout now lasts down to **800** raw dp — the width of that display at 100 % scaling — and only below it does anything shrink, in a deliberate order: the density steps down first (800 → 750 → 700 → 650), the right panel is given away below 800, and the sidebar, the last thing to go, collapses below 700. **Watch:** a 800x600 window must show the sidebar expanded, the right panel visible and the text at the user's own density; shrinking further must take the density, then the panel, then the sidebar, and growing back must restore all three.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.23: the full layout at 800x600, a room that opens first try, and suggestions that reach the queue

---
This release was built automatically from commit `2731f22107e3afdaebe1daf494623d0048a2cc77`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.22
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.22
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The sign-in window now waits for `LOGIN_INFO` instead of reading the cookie store once.** The user's `~/.vivimusic/login-debug.log` holds both outcomes of the same code path, seven seconds after the same visit: at `2026-10-08T16:52` the visit to `www.youtube.com` produced the cookie and the flow delivered a completed session, while at `2026-10-08T16:45` it came back with 35 cookies and no `LOGIN_INFO`, so the window handed over a **partial** session (which the log names: `delivering PARTIAL session, missing critical: [LOGIN_INFO]`), the account validation answered 401 and the app showed the `E1033` from issue #101 again. One fixed `Thread.sleep(7_000)` after one visit was deciding it. The visit is now made up to twice and the store is polled for up to 15 s after each one, stopping the moment the cookie appears and the log naming each visit (`after www.youtube.com (visit 1/2): N cookies, missing=[...]`), so a fast success is still fast and a slow one is no longer a coin toss. **Watch:** a successful sign-in must end with `after www.youtube.com (visit 1/2)` followed by `delivering completed session`, and a failure must name how many visits were tried before the partial hand-over. **Open sub-item:** the login window needs a display and a real Google account, so this is a log-driven fix that compiles and is reasoned from the two entries above; only a real sign-in confirms it.
